channel.title: BK Reader (The Brooklyn Reader) - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from BK Reader (The Brooklyn Reader) (bkreader.com)

item.title: Brooklyn is Over The Snow
item.description: Brooklynites weighed in after the last storm dumped 20 inches of snow on parts of the borough. Car owners were the loudest critics, citing poor street cleanup, but most residents said the city did a solid job restoring order.

item.title: Brooklyn Tenants Take a Stand at NYC’s First Rental Ripoff Hearing
item.description: Over 200 Brooklyn residents had three minutes to tell a city official about their housing complaint in Downtown Brooklyn.

item.title: Two Brooklyn Nonprofits Secure Anti-Hate Funding
item.description: Homecrest Community Services and the Jewish Community Council of Greater Coney Island received 2026 NYC Community Project Grants to combat hate and strengthen neighborhood ties.

item.title: Feb 28: Brooklyn Black History Maker, Elizabeth A. Gloucester
item.description: An abolitionist, land owner and business operator, Gloucester was said to be the wealthiest Black woman in the nation at the time of her death in 1883.

item.title: State Approves Key Contract in SUNY Downstate Hospital Rebuild
item.description: New York moves forward with a major SUNY Downstate overhaul, and as its first step, will demolish an old parking garage.

item.title: South Brooklyn Health CEO Tapped to Lead Maimonides Hospital
item.description: A new agreement will bring Maimonides into the NYC Health + Hospitals system, expanding access to care across Brooklyn.

item.title: Brooklyn Community Leaders Honored by Pop Smoke Foundation
item.description: Residents and community leaders gathered at The Bogart House for the Canarsie Honors, celebrating local changemakers and supporting youth initiatives through the Shoot For The Stars Foundation, a nonprofit tied to Pop Smoke.

item.title: Apply to Summer Rising 2026 For Free Summer Classes
item.description: Families can apply from March 3- 27 to access free summer programming for students in kindergarten through eighth grade.

item.title: Brooklyn Disability Advocate Named to State Advisory Council
item.description: Simcha Weinstein, a rabbi and autism advocate from Brooklyn, is named to New York’s Developmental Disabilities Council following years of statewide advocacy.

item.title: Brooklyn Public Library Hosts Engineers Week Youth Competition
item.description: Brooklyn teens spent their mid-winter break learning about energy conservation and equity, presenting animation, game design and digital art projects to National Grid engineers.
